thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in 5xx and tail latency from model variant goliath-v2-quant across multiple regions. Error rate > 8% for the last 3m, latency p95 ~ 3.2s. Paging oncall.
Devon: ack, I'm on it. Pulling logs and seeing degraded KV cache hits.
Devon: quick check — are we seeing tokenization OOMs or kernel failures?
Samir: logs show repeated CUDA OOM on hosts gpu-prod-12/13 around 16:03 UTC, then heavy retries.
Ashok: same for me — transformer kernel throws mem alloc errors then RPC retries pile up. Likely quantized execution path regression in the latest packaging.
Devon: triage plan: 1) throttle heavy API keys, 2) temporarily eject goliath-v2-quant from the routing table, 3) roll traffic to goliath-stable-v1 (safer) and enable emergency quotas.
Priya: calling it: customer impact potential for high-volume keys (CorpX, travelbot-prod). We should notify CS and use emergency quotas to protect platform.
Carla: @SupportBot please open a high-priority ticket for affected customers and add standard incident banner.
SupportBot: created ticket INC-2026-437 for customer notifications and added incident banner.
Devon: running routing eject command now (will paste).
Devon: ```bash
# remove variant from active routing pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" 
  https://api.redwood.internal/routing/variants/eject 
  -d '{"model":"goliath","variant":"v2-quant","reason":"runtime-oom-spike"}'
```
Samir: exec OK, response 202 accepted. Routing tables will converge in ~30s.
IncidentBot: routing-change: variant ejection queued by Devon (2026-03-15T16:07:12Z).
Devon: now applying emergency key-level quotas for top noisy keys. Using internal quota CLI.
Devon: ```json
# quota patch
{"patch": [{"key":"corpX-prod","qps":10},{"key":"travelbot-prod","qps":5}], "reason":"protect-cluster-during-incident"}
```
Priya: applying quotas... done. Confirmed drop in request arrival rate for those keys.
Samir: routing showed immediate drop in load to gpu-prod-12/13 but we still see retry storms from older client SDKs hitting the variant ID directly.
Devon: next step: we should enable a temporary compatibility redirect that maps variant id -> stable variant for any direct calls. Priya can you flip that?
Priya: flipping compatibility redirect to goliath-stable-v1 for variant id "goliath-v2-quant". Command: `routectl map-variant --from goliath-v2-quant --to goliath-stable-v1 --ttl 600`
Priya: done. Logs show clients now resolving to stable variant.
Carla: CS updated customers: "We've routed traffic to a stable variant and applied temporary quotas; you may see degraded throughput for a few minutes. We're continuing to investigate."
Devon: monitoring: error rate falling to 0.9% and p95 back under 600ms for most routes. GPU OOM logs stopped after ejection.
Ashok: good signal. We should pin goliath-stable-v1 as fallback in the rollout policy and mark v2-quant as quarantined.
Devon: marking quarantined and creating follow-up ticket for root cause: packaging/quantization-change.
Samir: creating RCA ticket now: INFRA-7821, tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.
IncidentBot: note: automatic canary demote executed by the platform because of error budget breach.
Devon: handing off to Priya for next shift / monitoring and follow-up. Summary: ejected goliath-v2-quant, applied emergency quotas for noisy keys, enabled compatibility redirect to goliath-stable-v1, CS notified. Impact: short period of higher latency and errors for CorpX and travelbot-prod; mitigation reduced impact within ~6 minutes.
Priya: taking over. I'll coordinate with eng-ml to validate quantized kernels and schedule a safe redeploy window. Priya: action items — reproduce locally on quantized runner, add more aggressive preflight checks, add circuit-breaker on variant-level error budget.
Carla: putting a post-incident note in the incidents channel and scheduling a 1-hr postmortem tomorrow.
Devon: one more note — found a handful of direct client retries in logs with hardcoded variant; recommend client SDK patch to respect routing redirects.
Samir: can we add a short-term server-side redirect TTL extension so older clients won't keep hitting quarantined variant?
Priya: set TTL to 3600s for safety. Done.
IncidentBot: incident closed for active mitigation; follow-ups: INFRA-7821, ENG-ML-234.
Carla: :thumbsup: great work. Will add owners and due dates in the postmortem.
Priya: handoff complete — I'm monitoring for 30 more minutes then will update the oncall rotation.
Devon: thanks everyone.
SupportBot: summary message posted to customers and internal status page. Ticket INC-2026-437 updated.
Carla: end of thread.
